Of the properties of morphisms which are stable under base change
(as listed in
Remark <REF_0001>)
the following are also <TEXTITOPEN_0001>stable under compositions<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> closed, open and locally closed immersions, see
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0002>,
<STRUCT_0003> quasi-compact, see
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0003>,
<STRUCT_0004> universally closed, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0004>,
<STRUCT_0005> (quasi-)separated, see
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0005>,
<STRUCT_0006> monomorphism, see
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0006>,
<STRUCT_0007> surjective, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0007>,
<STRUCT_0008> universally injective, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0008>,
<STRUCT_0009> affine, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0009>,
<STRUCT_0010> quasi-affine, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0010>,
<STRUCT_0011> (locally) of finite type, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0011>,
<STRUCT_0012> (locally) quasi-finite, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0012>,
<STRUCT_0013> (locally) of finite presentation, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0013>,
<STRUCT_0014> universally open, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0014>,
<STRUCT_0015> flat, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0015>,
<STRUCT_0016> syntomic, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0016>,
<STRUCT_0017> smooth, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0017>,
<STRUCT_0018> unramified (resp.<SPACE_0001>G-unramified), see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0018>,
<STRUCT_0019> <ACCENT_0001>tale, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0019>,
<STRUCT_0020> proper, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0020>,
<STRUCT_0021> H-projective, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0021>,
<STRUCT_0022> finite or integral, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0022>,
<STRUCT_0023> finite locally free, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0023>,
<STRUCT_0024> universally submersive, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0024>,
<STRUCT_0025> universal homeomorphism, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0025>.
<STRUCT_0026>
Add more as needed.

Of the properties mentioned which are stable under base change
(as listed in Remark <REF_0001>)
the following are also <TEXTITOPEN_0001>fpqc local on the base<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
(and a fortiori fppf local on the base):
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> for immersions we have this for
<STRUCT_0003>
<STRUCT_0004> closed immersions, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0002>,
<STRUCT_0005> open immersions, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0003>, and
<STRUCT_0006> quasi-compact immersions, see
Descent,
Lemma <REF_0004>,
<STRUCT_0007>
<STRUCT_0008> quasi-compact, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0005>,
<STRUCT_0009> universally closed, see
Descent, Lemma
<REF_0006>,
<STRUCT_0010> (quasi-)separated, see
Descent, Lemmas
<REF_0007>, and
<REF_0008>,

Descent, Lemma <REF_0011>,
<STRUCT_0014> affine, see

<STRUCT_0015> quasi-affine, see

<STRUCT_0018> (locally) of finite presentation, see
Descent, Lemmas
<REF_0017>, and
<REF_0018>,

Descent,
Lemma <REF_0019>,

<STRUCT_0021> flat, see

<STRUCT_0025> <ACCENT_0001>tale, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0025>,
<STRUCT_0026> proper, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0026>,
<STRUCT_0027> finite or integral, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0027>,
<STRUCT_0028> finite locally free, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0028>,
<STRUCT_0029> universally submersive, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0029>,
<STRUCT_0030> universal homeomorphism, see
Descent, Lemma <REF_0030>.
<STRUCT_0031>
Note that the property of being an ``immersion'' may not be fpqc local
on the base, but in
Descent, Lemma <REF_0031>
we proved that it is fppf local on the base.
